newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks seen higher at start.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks seen higher at start.

text.p: U.S. stocks are expected to open higher Monday, with investors focusing on brokerages after news of the definitive merger agreement between Bankers Trust New York Corp and Alex. Brown Inc.
"This is an important element," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities.

"(Merger) deals are running ahead of last year, and last year was a record. Investors will be looking at Legg Mason, PaineWebber and other companies that might be eligible for a deal with a major bank."
Bankers Trust and Alex. Brown said on Sunday they had signed a definitive agreement to merge in a stock swap valued at about $1.7 billion.
Under terms of the deal, which was unanimously approved by both companies' boards, each Alex. Brown common share would be exchanged for 0.83 shares of Bankers Trust common stock, the companies said.
Wachtel said that momentum from Friday would carry the Dow industrials higher at the start, backed by a strong dollar, steady bonds and higher European markets.
"We have a decent background for a decent opening," he said, adding that investors would keep an eye on the long bond yield as it edged towards 7.15 percent, the 1996 high.
Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments, said that strength in high technologies saved the market Friday and could move it higher today.

"There is room for techs to move higher as we await the earnings reports. It was the over-the-counter market which led us lower on fears of an interest rate hike, and it is the OTC market which will help the overall market stabilize," he said.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei Average was down 144.92 points, or 0.81 percent, at 17,715.67.
In London, the FTSE 100 Index was up 26.3 at 4262.9.

U.S. shares traded in London were mostly firmer. Boeing Co was up 1/2 at 98-1/2 after a report in the Wall Street Journal said the company planned to boost its production rate for all planes by 10 percent beyond previously announced levels. Oil stocks, which took a hammering last week due to the weak crude price, were moderately higher. Exxon Corp was up 3/8 at 102 while Texaco Inc gained 1/2 to 104.
Among the high techs, Motorola Inc, due to report first quarter earnings after the close of trading today, was 1/4 higher at 60 while International Business Machines Corp was up 3/8 at 129-1/2.
The dollar was firm but off its highs in Tokyo and hit a fresh four-year high against the yen in Europe.
U.S. Treasuries were higher, with the long bond up 5/32 to yield 7.11 percent.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street writes that some investors thought the oil giants would offer a safe harbor from market turbulence. Instead, they've offered more turbulence.
